name: Banana Bread Butter

ingredients.name: ripe but firm medium bananas, peeled and halved lengthwise

instructions.primary_message: In a large 30-cm stainless-steel skillet over medium-high heat, melt 4 tablespoons butter with brown sugar, salt, cinnamon, and cardamom while stirring and swirling, until butter is melted and mixture blends into a grainy liquid and begins to bubble, about 2 minutes. Add bananas, cut side down, and continue to cook, swirling gently, until liquid begins to resemble a smoother caramel, about 2 minutes longer.

Add rum (do not pour directly from the bottle if working over an open flame), then tilt pan to ignite the alcohol from a gas burner, or carefully light with a match. Cook, shaking the pan, until the flames have died out and the caramel has thickened to a honey consistency, about 1 to 2 minutes. Alternatively, you can add the rum and not light it on fire, instead simmering until the rum has mostly cooked off and the caramel has reached a honey consistency.

In a food processor, place banana mixture, almond butter, vanilla, and remaining 12 tablespoons butter and process until smooth and combined, about 1 minute. Serve immediately on pancakes, toast, biscuits, and more; or transfer to an airtight container and store in the refrigerator for up to 2 weeks.

description: This banana bread butter blends caramelized bananas, rum, and warm spices into a sweet, nutty spread. Inspired by a combination of banana bread and bananas Foster, it's quick to make, keeps well in the fridge for two weeks, and perfect for topping pancakes, toast, waffles, and more.
notes:
Notes: A dark rum, such as Myers's, works especially well here, adding a rich, robust flavor that melds seamlessly with the warm spices.

Make-ahead and storage: Butter can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 2 weeks.
author: Kelli Solomon
